title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Find the Fastest Route!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra slice travel time by searching from both the start and destination at the same time. As the two frontiers meet, the shortest path emerges with fewer explored streets than classic one-way search.
ig_caption:
🗺️✨ In Tbilisi’s Vake Park area, Bidirectional Dijkstra hunts the shortest route by running two synchronized Dijkstra searches: one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal. ⚡

🧠 Tech breakdown: instead of expanding outward from only one side, we maintain two priority queues and their distance maps (g₍s→v₎ and g₍t→v₎). Each step grows the frontier from the currently best candidate (lowest tentative distance), and the algorithm stops when the best combined path found so far is ≤ the smallest possible distance that could still be improved. ✅

📍Graph theory on real street maps: your city roads become a weighted graph where edges represent street segments (optionally with distance, travel time, or turn penalties). Bidirectional Dijkstra leverages symmetry (reversing edges for the backward search) so the “search effort” spreads from both ends, often reducing explored nodes dramatically. 🌉
